steps.title: Prepare Discovery Ultra reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare all reagents and antibody dispensers for the Ventana Discovery Ultra according to the listed concentrations and loading instructions.

substeps.instruction: Dilute DISCOVERY Wash 10× stock to 1× with Milli‑Q water and load into the reservoir.
Dilute Reaction Buffer Concentrate 10× to 1× with Milli‑Q water and load into the reservoir.
Load Liquid Cover Slip (LCS) into the reservoir.
Load Benchmark Ultra CC1 into the reservoir.
Load Benchmark Ultra CC2 into the reservoir.
Load Option Reservoir with Reaction Buffer (not used).
Load DISCOVERY Inhibitor (ready‑to‑use) into the dispenser.
Prepare Pretreatment 1: dissolve Copper Sulfate to 50 mM in Milli‑Q water and load (optional for formalin‑fixed tissue).
Dilute Granzyme B 1:100 in Antibody Diluent and load into Antibody 1 dispenser (final on‑slide concentration will be 1:400).
Dilute FOXP3 1:100 in Antibody Diluent and load into Antibody 2 dispenser (final on‑slide 1:400).
Dilute CD8 1:100 in Antibody Diluent and load into Antibody 3 dispenser (final on‑slide 1:400).
Dilute CD4 1:200 in Antibody Diluent and load into Antibody 4 dispenser (final on‑slide 1:800).
Load PanCK ready‑to‑use reagent into its dispenser.
Dilute Ki67 1:100 in Antibody Diluent and load into Antibody 5 dispenser (final on‑slide 1:400).
Dilute Opal 480 1:100 in 1× Amplification Diluent and load into Detection 1 dispenser.
Dilute Opal 520 1:100 in 1× Amplification Diluent and load into Detection 2 dispenser.
Dilute Opal 570 1:100 in 1× Amplification Diluent and load into Detection 3 dispenser.
Dilute Opal 620 1:100 in 1× Amplification Diluent and load into Detection 4 dispenser.
Dilute Opal 690 1:100 in 1× Amplification Diluent and load into Detection 5 dispenser.
Dilute TSA‑DIG 1:100 in 1× Amplification Diluent and load into Detection 6 dispenser.
Dilute Opal 780 1:12.5 in Antibody Diluent and load into Detection 7 dispenser.
Load OmniMAP Anti‑Rat HRP (ready‑to‑use) into its dispenser.
Load OmniMAP Anti‑Rabbit HRP (ready‑to‑use) into its dispenser.
Load OmniMAP Anti‑Mouse HRP (ready‑to‑use) into its dispenser.
Prepare Counterstain 1: add 3 drops of Akoya DAPI to 1 mL Milli‑Q water and load.

steps.title: Deparaffinize slides
steps.instruction: Remove paraffin and rehydrate tissue sections before staining.

substeps.instruction: Bake slides for 32 min at 69 °C.
Deparaffinize slides with DISCOVERY Wash for 32 min at 69 °C.

steps.title: Antigen retrieval & quenching
steps.instruction: Retrieve antigens and quench background fluorescence using CC1, copper sulfate, and DISCOVERY Inhibitor.

substeps.instruction: Incubate slides with Cell Conditioner 1 (CC1, Tris‑based, pH 7.0–9.2) for 32 min at 95 °C.
Incubate slides with 50 mM Copper Sulfate for 1 h at 37 °C.
Incubate slides with DISCOVERY Inhibitor for 16 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Primary‑secondary‑tyramide cycle
steps.instruction: Perform sequential primary antibody incubation, secondary HRP, tyramide amplification, and CC2 for each marker according to Table 1.

substeps.instruction: For each primary antibody (Granzyme B, FOXP3, CD8, CD4, PanCK, Ki67):
Incubate with the primary antibody at 37 °C for the time listed (Granzyme B, FOXP3, CD8, CD4, PanCK: 32 min; Ki67: 16 min).
Incubate with the appropriate secondary HRP (Anti‑Rabbit for Granzyme B, FOXP3, Ki67; Anti‑Rat for CD8, CD4; Anti‑Mouse for PanCK) for 16 min at 37 °C.
Incubate with the corresponding Opal tyramide (Granzyme B → Opal 520; FOXP3 → Opal 690; CD8 → Opal 620; CD4 → Opal 570; PanCK → Opal 480; Ki67 → TSA‑DIG) for 16 min at 37 °C.
Incubate in Cell Conditioner 2 for 8 min at 95 °C.
Repeat the above sub‑steps for each of the six primary antibodies.

steps.title: Stain with Opal 780
steps.instruction: Apply the final Opal 780 tyramide to label the TSA‑DIG signal.

substeps.instruction: After the last Cell Conditioner 2 incubation, incubate slides in Opal 780 for 1 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: DAPI counterstain and mount
steps.instruction: Counterstain nuclei, wash, and mount slides for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Incubate slides in DAPI solution for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove slides from the Ventana autostainer, wash off LCS thoroughly with 5 % Dawn dish soap and rinse with water.
Apply 50–100 µL per slide of Prolong Gold Antifade Mountant.
Place coverslip and harden for ≥1 h at 20–25 °C protected from light.
Store slides at 4 °C protected from light for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Acquire whole‑slide images
steps.instruction: Capture multispectral fluorescence images of the stained slides.

substeps.instruction: Use a Vectra Polaris or equivalent platform capable of ≥7 fluorescence channels to acquire whole‑slide images.

steps.title: Select ROIs and export
steps.instruction: Identify representative regions and export image data for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open images in Phenochart (or QuPath), review, select regions of interest, and batch‑export fields.

steps.title: Spectral unmixing
steps.instruction: Separate overlapping fluorophores and remove autofluorescence.

substeps.instruction: Perform spectral unmixing with inForm (or QuPath) using a pre‑built spectral library; linear unmixing is also possible in QuPath.

steps.title: Stitch image tiles
steps.instruction: Assemble unmixed tiles into a full‑resolution whole‑slide image.

substeps.instruction: Use HALO or QuPath to stitch tiles together.

steps.title: Classify tissue vs glass
steps.instruction: Generate a classifier to separate tissue from background.

substeps.instruction: Run the Halo Tissue Classifier Module (or equivalent in QuPath) to create a tissue mask.

steps.title: Detect nuclei and segment cells
steps.instruction: Perform nuclear detection and cell segmentation using DAPI with the parameters in Table 2.

substeps.instruction: Set Nuclear Contrast Threshold = 0.5.
Set Minimum Nuclear Intensity = 0.1.
Set Maximum Image Brightness = 0.1.
Set Nuclear Segmentation Aggressiveness = 0.7.
Set Fill Nuclear Holes = False.
Set Nuclear Size = 1,482.3009.
Set Minimum Nuclear Roundness = 0.
Set Number of Nuclear Dyes = 1 (DAPI).
Set Nuclear D1 Weight = 1.
Run detection in HALO (or Inform, QuPath, Fiji).

steps.title: Set Opal intensity thresholds
steps.instruction: Define positivity thresholds for each Opal channel.

substeps.instruction: For Opal 570 (CD4) set positive range 1.5–11.
Set Nucleus % Completeness = 0.14.
Define analogous thresholds for the remaining Opal channels based on control regions.

steps.title: Assign cell phenotypes
steps.instruction: Classify each segmented cell into phenotypic categories using Table 3.

substeps.instruction: Use HALO (or Inform, QuPath, Fiji) to apply the marker‑positive/negative logic shown in Table 3 (e.g., CD4+ T Cell = Opal 480−, Opal 520−, Opal 570+, Opal 620−, Opal 690−, Opal 780−).
Generate phenotype labels for CD4+ T Cell, CD8+ T Cell, PanCK+ tumor cell, CD4+ FOXP3+, CD8+ Granzyme B+, CD4+ Ki67+, CD8+ Ki67+, PanCK+ Ki67+, etc.

steps.title: Quantify cell populations
steps.instruction: Measure the abundance of each phenotype across the whole slide.

substeps.instruction: Run whole‑slide quantification in HALO (or export single‑cell data to QuPath or CSV for downstream analysis).

steps.title: Annotate tumor border
steps.instruction: Define tumor regions based on PanCK staining to create a border annotation.

substeps.instruction: In HALO (or QuPath), use PanCK signal to delineate tumor versus stroma and generate a tumor border mask.

steps.title: Perform spatial infiltration analysis
steps.instruction: Assess intratumoral and peritumoral distribution of each cell type.

substeps.instruction: In the HALO Spatial Analysis Module (or equivalent), generate concentric 200 µm bands inside (intratumoral) and outside (peritumoral) the tumor border.
Calculate cell‑type densities within each band for all phenotypes.

description: Accurate spatial characterization of T cell subsets within tumors is essential for understanding antitumor immunity and therapeutic responsiveness. Distinct T cell states (i.e., cytotoxic effector T cells, regulatory T cells, and proliferating subsets) play divergent roles in tumor progression, immune evasion, and response to immunotherapies. Their spatial organization, density, and interactions with tumor and stromal cells can strongly influence outcomes in approaches, such as immune checkpoint blockade and other T cell–dependent treatments. Consequently, experimental workflows that preserve tissue context while enabling reliable discrimination among T cell functional states are increasingly important. This protocol provides a streamlined method for 7-plex immunofluorescent staining of murine tumor sections, enabling simultaneous visualization of multiple T cell markers alongside nuclear segmentation and functional readouts (Figure 1). When integrated with spatial analysis pipelines, the resulting datasets support the generation of quantitative maps of T cell distribution, infiltration patterns, and cell–cell interactions across the tumor microenvironment. This approach avoids the extensive panel development and analytical burden associated with many spatial omics platforms while still allowing efficient processing of multiple tumor regions to obtain a comprehensive view of T cell behavior. These spatial maps can reveal T cell–dense zones, the balance between effector and regulatory subsets, and proximity relationships with tumor or stromal compartments, providing insight into T cell activation, exhaustion, and suppressive states while complementing single-cell sequencing datasets by validating cell–cell relationships directly within intact tissue.
